Regular Council Meeting CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
JOINT
REGULAR
MEETING
WEDNESDAY, MAY 28, 2008
06:00 P.M.
CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
635 S. HIGHWAY 101
SOLANA BEACH, CALIFORNIA
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 at least 48 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24.
A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library the Friday before each Council meeting and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item that are received after the distribution of the agenda and before 4:30 p.m. on the meeting day will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

1.
Public Notification Service
Mayor Kellejian introduced the presentation and stated that there had been some changes in the City’s e-blast service in order to dedicate a section for emergency information.
Steve Didier, Management Analyst, presented a power point presentation on the City's e-blast service. He stated that it was an e-mail service, that the public could sign up on the City's website, that there was information distributed on items such as the Council agenda, employement, and special events. He stated that each e-mail sent out allowed the receiver to unscubscribe to the service and that there were 1,100 people currently subscribed for the e-blast service.
Council discussion ensued regarding the e-blast service, that residents were encouraged to sign up for the service, that it was helpful to receive information regarding City events, that it was used for City business, and that there should be a disclaimer added that e-mail addresses would not be sold to others.

Please be aware of the three-minute timer light on the Council Dais.
10.
Fiscal Year 2008-09 Resolution of Fees. (File 0390-20)
Recommendation: Recommendation: That the City Council
A.
Find Report Council disclosures.
B.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, Receive public testimony, Close the public hearing.
C.
Adopt Resolution 2008-080 establishing a new schedule of fees and charges for City services for FY 2008-09.
Item 10 Report (click here)
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item. He stated that the user fees were last updated in 2007 and prior to that updated in 1996. He stated that a study was conducted to analyze fees, that user fees should be updated annually to compare with the consumer price index, and that some fees would not be changed.
Steve Didier, Management Analyst, presented a power point presentation on the user fee study. He stated that some fees would not be changing which included, document printing, audio video production services, notary, and certification of documents. He stated that there would not be an increase in fees for summer camps, for the Junior Lifeguard Program, or for building plan checks or inspection fees. He stated that user fee increase would match the 2.3% consumer price index.
Council discussion ensued regarding fees on the Junior Lifeguard Program, that there would still be full cost recovery without raising costs, whether businesses could use City facilities and make a profit without paying fees for the use of facilities, and how certain programs were overseen at La Colonia Park.
Council discussion ensued regarding whether the user fees for the View Assessment process would be increased and that even an increase of 2.3% would still not be cost recovery for the view assessment process fees.
Council discussion ensued regarding not increasing the view assessment filing fees, that not raising the fee would allow the process to be accessible to the public, and that Council could evaluate this fee annually to determine whether an increase would be desired.
Mayor Kellejian opened the public hearing.
MOTION: Moved by Campbell and seconded by Roberts to approve to close the public hearing. Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Campbell and seconded by Roberts to approve staff recommendation to adopt the User Fees with the exception of the View Assessment Fees and to evaluate user fee increases annually. Motion carried unanimously.

Item 12 Report (click here)
Item 12 documents distributed after the agenda posting
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item. He stated that there would be concerts at Fletcher Cove Park every Thursday evening in the summer for 12 weeks, that the event would be family oriented, and that the City would partner with the Belly Up to provide entertainment.
Kirk Wenger, Parks and Recreation Supervisor, presented a power point presentation regarding a pilot project for a new summer concert series called "Concerts at the Cove." He stated that event would consist of local amatuer musicians, that the event would be family friendly entertainment, that artists had been tentatively booked, and that City park rules would be enforced during the concerts. He stated that the City would approve appropriate musicians for the venue, that staff had drafted a promotional flyer, and that the event would provide the opportunity for community unity.
Council discussion ensued regarding the proposal, whether there would be a cancellation policy, that no dogs would be allowed at the park during the concerts, that additional amplification towards the ocean may be needed, that it was a positive event for the City, that there would be county health requirements for providing food at the event, and that the first year would be considered a trial period.
